title: Discovery call that shifts to data residency
purpose: Explore reporting needs for a retail analytics pilot

turns.text: Which reports does your team open every week?
Mostly the weekly sales by store and the stock-outs report.
Forecasts, we only see what already happened.
But honestly, before any pilot, legal will ask where the data is stored. Last year they killed a pilot because the vendor hosted outside the EU.
They also want to know whether customer loyalty IDs leave our systems at all.

mustInclude: Follows the shift to legal and data residency rather than returning to reports
Asks something that would clarify what legal needs to approve, e.g. which exact requirement ended last year's pilot, or whether pseudonymised loyalty IDs would be acceptable
mustNotInclude: Asks again which reports the team uses
Asserts where the vendor stores data
checkpoints.ideal: Ask what exactly legal required last year, EU hosting only or also no loyalty IDs leaving, so the pilot can be scoped to pass.

mustInclude: Offers a grounded angle on reducing the legal blocker (e.g. aggregating at store level so loyalty IDs never leave)
Marks general-knowledge suggestions as uncertain rather than as facts about this vendor
mustNotInclude: States a specific certification or hosting location of the vendor as fact
checkpoints.ideal: Suggest scoping the pilot on store-level aggregates without loyalty IDs, so the residency question narrows to aggregated data.
